best_for: People who already pay for storage such as Backblaze B2, S3 or a NAS and want free, encrypted, scheduled file backups of their computer with a window to click through.
description:
KopiaUI is the desktop app for Kopia, an open-source backup tool from the Kopia Project, released under the Apache 2.0 license. The name is Polish for "copy". The same engine also runs from the command line if you prefer typing commands.

After the first snapshot, Kopia uploads only what changed. When you edit a huge file, just the changed parts go up, and a file you move or rename is not sent again. You can leave chosen files and folders out, add error correction, and check that your backups are still sound. Several computers can share one repository, but there is one password per repository and no per-user access, so share it only with people you trust.

points.title: You supply the storage
points.text: Kopia has no cloud of its own. Snapshots go to S3 or S3-compatible services, Azure, Backblaze B2, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP, WebDAV, a local or network drive, or your own Kopia server. You pay that provider, not Kopia.

points.title: Encrypted, compressed, deduplicated
points.text: Snapshots are encrypted on your machine before upload, and deduplication stores repeated data once, which keeps storage bills down.

points.title: Lose the password, lose the backups
points.text: The docs are blunt: there is no way to restore files from a repository if you forget its password. Store it somewhere safe outside the backup.

points.title: Files and folders, not disk images
points.text: Kopia backs up the folders you pick. It does not image a whole drive for bare-metal restore. To get files back you can mount a snapshot as a drive, restore it all, or download single files.

points.title: Schedules and retention
points.text: Set a snapshot frequency in a policy and KopiaUI takes snapshots on its own. Policies also set how many hourly, daily, weekly, monthly and yearly snapshots to keep.

points.title: Rclone support is experimental
points.text: Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive work through Rclone, but the project calls this experimental and says other Rclone services may not work.

points.title: Install options
points.text: KopiaUI needs 64-bit Windows 10 or later; the installer can install per-user or for all users. The Windows listing keeps 38 versions; macOS lists only the current release. Linux is not listed here; Kopia offers APT and YUM repositories.
